disposition_reason: Published monkey-specific projected-fit anchors exist, but the exact empirical population, projection/error normalization, trial membership and model-to-neural adapter are not recoverable as one verified comparison. The current fixed-original-neuron scorer uses a new metric and nested split; its improvement is an extension and cannot surpass the paper's projected R-squared.

source_paper.title: Latent circuit inference from heterogeneous neural responses during cognitive tasks

evidence.locator: Results: Representations of irrelevant stimuli in the PFC; Figure 6 and Extended Data Figures 7-9
evidence.supports: Original two-monkey empirical task reports projected test R-squared 0.88/0.76 and captured total variance 11%/7%; fit-quality and connectivity summaries use different fit aggregations.

evidence.locator: Methods: Analysis of PFC data, equations 28-32; Statistics and reproducibility
evidence.supports: Original half-trial design, preprocessing, eligibility, three-term empirical objective and 200 initializations per monkey. Methods and Results report different unit counts; printed loss does not by itself resolve reported R-squared implementation.

evidence.locator: latent_net.py lines 79-104, loss and normalized-error helpers
evidence.supports: Released class uses mse_z + l_y*nmse_y; projected diagnostic normalization uses centered full-dimensional data variance. It does not establish the paper's empirical fitted-intercept/three-term objective or sampling adapter.
Inspected release demonstrates a trained-RNN tutorial; a complete original empirical-PFC entry point was not established.

evidence.locator: Mante et al. 2013 data page: PFC data.zip and tdr.zip
evidence.supports: Original neural-data and targeted-dimensionality-reduction archive routes exist. Archive payload, trial membership and eligibility were not read or authenticated in this audit.

target.description: Infer a compact recurrent circuit accounting for the original two-monkey PFC condition-averaged responses and native context-dependent task output, retaining all 72 stimulus/context conditions.

dataset.description: Original Mante et al. 2013 PFC dataset used by the paper, with public PFC data.zip and tdr.zip routes; exact archive identity and empirical adapter remain admission blockers.

cohort.description: Both monkeys A and F are required. Results lists 727/574 PFC units; Methods lists 762/640 available and 483/323 meeting at least four correct trials in every condition. These denominators require source/data reconciliation; none may be chosen for convenience.

split.description: Original condition-wise disjoint equal half-trial train/validation averages must be recovered with their trial membership. The local train/validation/assessment partition is a different experiment, not the paper's original split.

inputs.description: Original unit-level correct-trial neural responses, 2 x 6 x 6 context/motion/color condition identities, and native continuous task-output targets. Non-simultaneous units cannot be treated as synchronized population trials.

preprocessing.description: Published processing includes 50-ms bins, 40-ms Gaussian smoothing, split-specific z-scoring, condition-independent mean subtraction and PCA retaining 50% variance. The 15 neural samples versus 150 model steps of 10 ms and empirical intercept/loss adapter are unbound.

metric.description: Paper reports projected test R-squared, but equations 31-32 print normalized norm-based error terms and the released diagnostic helper uses a different variance normalization. Recover exact centering, squaring and conversion to reported R-squared; a standard formula cannot be assumed.

aggregation.description: Keep A and F separate. Extended Data 7a/8a describes means over 200 fits with bootstrap intervals; top-ten fits in Figure 6b/Extended Data 9b summarize connectivity weights. The exact relationship of rounded 0.88/0.76 to score-producing fit aggregates remains unbound.

comparison.primary_metric: Original monkey-specific projected test R-squared with total-variance capture and native task-output fit retained

published_baseline.description: 0.88 is the reported monkey-A anchor only; monkey F is 0.76. The paper also reports captured total PFC variance of 11% and 7%, respectively. No pooled scalar baseline is asserted; original score normalization and full fit distribution must be recovered.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: No native complete two-monkey empirical replay is established. The trained-RNN tutorial and new fixed-neuron scorer are neither the source empirical reference nor equivalent numerical baselines.

minimum_effect.rationale: A meaningful projected-fit improvement cannot be declared until the original denominator, projection constraints and captured-variance/continuous-behavior safeguards are fixed. A universal R-squared margin would be unsupported.

uncertainty.method: Recover original 200-fit distributions, then predeclare paired comparison and stochastic-selection accounting. Report each monkey separately and distinguish conditional trial/session uncertainty from optimization variability.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Two biological monkeys; trial/session units require verified recording hierarchy; optimizer starts are not animals
uncertainty.rationale: The paper's bootstrap across fitted models describes fit variation, not 200 biological replications. New inferential thresholds and aggregation cannot be inferred from that interval.

paper_win_requires: Recover exact empirical census, half-trial membership, timing adapter, objective, projection and reported-score formula before comparing methods.
Retain both monkeys and every original eligible unit/condition; compare monkey A with its 0.88 anchor and monkey F with its 0.76 anchor at original source precision under the same protocol.
Predeclare meaningful improvement and uncertainty while retaining captured-variance and native continuous task-output safeguards; increasing fit in an easier learned projection alone is insufficient.
Preserve the complete 200-initialization-per-monkey reference and declared selection policy, including failed starts; do not confuse all-fit score aggregation with top-ten connectivity summaries.
Treat fixed-original-neuron loss, new nested or condition-blocked splits and binary choice accuracy as separately labelled extensions; none is interchangeable with published projected R-squared.
Larger inferred suppression or smaller Mann-Whitney p-values cannot constitute method-performance improvement.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA comparison is established for the original empirical task.

episode.improvement_loop: Inactive pending source recovery. A future same-task episode must expose only source-compatible training/development feedback while preserving original comparison identities and preventing transfer of owner reference targets.
episode.candidate_freeze: Freeze circuit family, projection constraints, loss, optimizer, complete seed/start policy and preprocessing before assessment; exact original selection boundaries must be recovered first.
episode.final_evaluation: Use the recovered native two-monkey evaluator and original trial partition, report original fit distributions and monkey-specific neural/task outcomes. The current fixed-neuron assessment produces extension results only.
episode.baseline_policy: The published 0.88/0.76 anchors are distinct from a future author-method rerun and any current SOTA. A local reconstructed reference is not author-equivalent until empirical objective/timing and source-score parity are verified.

blocking_issues: Reconcile Results and Methods unit denominators using the complete original archive census without narrowing either monkey.
Recover original exact half-trial assignments and the native 150-step model to 15-sample neural clock/intercept/three-term loss adapter.
Resolve reported projected R-squared formula and normalization versus equations 31-32 and released helper code.
Bind original 200-fit distributions and score aggregation; the current top-ten connectivity summary cannot stand in for fit-quality aggregation.
Qualify source-compatible projection safeguards, meaningful effect, independent-unit uncertainty, candidate access and concrete cumulative resource/search budgets.

legacy.notes: Preserve initial-evaluator-v1 and its engineering controls. Its fixed-neuron normalized squared error and nested outer-trial split are a prospective scientific extension, not the source-paper success condition or an author-baseline replay.
